en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Worthy Head (Bhadramukha), one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Shengjian of the Western Qin.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Magadha at the place of the Seat of Pure Dharma. At that time...
At that time, a great assembly of bodhisattvas, including Maitreya Bodhisattva and others, as well as bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and asuras, gathered together.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Today, the Buddhas of the ten directions are also holding great assemblies to preach the sutras for the sake of the bodhisattvas.
Within the pure Dharma-seat, there was a laywoman named Bhadrasrī, who was the consort of King Bimbisāra; she joined her palms and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“I wish to hear the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions, as well as the names of the bodhisattvas and their buddha-fields.
The Buddha said,
“Excellent!”
Excellent!
I shall explain it for you.
In the eastern direction there is a Buddha named Entry into Diligence; his land is named Holding the Kīla Tree, and a bodhisattva there is named Reverent Head.
In the south there is a Buddha named Unremitting Joyful Diligence; his land is named World-Mind Tree, and his bodhisattva is named Awakening Head.
In the west there is a Buddha named Long Diligence; his land is named Lotus Tree, and his bodhisattva is named Jewel Head.
In the north there is a Buddha named Sūryavīra; his land is named Kharjūrīvṛkṣa, and his bodhisattva is named Dānaśīrṣa.
In the northeast there is a Buddha named Karuṇāvīra; his land is named Utpalavṛkṣa, and his bodhisattva is named Puṇyaśīrṣa.
To the southeast is a Buddha named Śata-vīrya, whose land is named Gandhavṛkṣa; his bodhisattva is named Mukha-saṃcodaka.
To the southwest is a Buddha named Uttama-vīrya, whose land is named Ratnavṛkṣa; his bodhisattva is named Vīryamukha.
To the northwest is a Buddha named Once-Vigorous, whose land is called Tree of Contemplation; his bodhisattva is named Good Chief.
Below is a Buddha named Brahma-Vigorous, whose land is called Water-Crystal Tree; his bodhisattva is named Wisdom Chief.

When Bhadrapāla heard the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions, as well as the names of the bodhisattvas and their buddha-fields, he leaped for joy with great delight. He prostrated himself before the Buddha, touching his head to the ground in salutation, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Although I have now resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, by what practice shall I leave behind this human body born of my mother?"
The Buddha said:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
"This is what the Buddha asked. The Buddha said, "Bhadraśrī!"
By practicing ten matters, one may escape the body of a mother.
By practicing one of these matters, one will swiftly attain manhood and personally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What is this one thing?
It is that by generating the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*), one performs immeasurable merits and is able not to forget them.
This is the one thing.
"Furthermore, there are two things by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What are these two things?
First, to act in accordance with one's words, not serving celestial deities but taking refuge solely in the Buddhas;
second, to act without believing in what is false.
These are the two matters.
"Furthermore, there are three things by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What are these three things?
First, constantly purifying and protecting the three [actions] of the body;
second, purifying and protecting the four [actions] of the mouth;
third, purifying and protecting the three [actions] of the mind.
These are the three matters.
Furthermore, there are four matters by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
What are the four matters?
First, being without flattery or deceit regarding what is given;
second, being without flattery or deceit regarding the precepts.
Third, maintaining one's own purity;
fourth, listening to the six dharmas without flattery or deceit.
These are the four matters.
"Furthermore, there are five things by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
What are these five things?
First, by means of the Dharma;
second, acting in accordance with the Dharma;
third, dwelling directly within the Dharma upon hearing it.
Fourth, not delighting in the body of a woman;
fifth, maintaining the thought of becoming a man.
These are the five matters.
"Furthermore, there are six matters by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What are these six matters?
First, not being indolent in one's actions and remaining mindful;
second, having a supple mind;
third, being simple and honest.
Fourth, he is not sycophantic or deceitful;
fifth, he is free from affectation;
sixth, his actions are characterized by utmost sincerity.
These are the six matters.
Furthermore, there are seven matters by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What are the seven?
First, constantly mindfulness of the Buddha as the Dharma-body;
second, constantly mindfulness of the Dharma to attain the wisdom of a Buddha;
Third, constantly mindfulness of the Sangha, which serves as a support;
fourth, constantly mindfulness of the precepts, through which purity is sought;
fifth, constantly mindfulness of giving, by which all defilements are removed.
Sixth, constantly mindfulness of the devas, which brings about the bodhisattva mind;
seventh, constantly mindfulness of humans, because of the desire to deliver all beings.
These are the seven matters.
"Furthermore, there are eight things by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What are these eight?
First, one does not take pleasure in food or clothing;
second, one does not [take pleasure] in flowers;
third, one does not [take pleasure] in incense.
Fourth, one should not use various blended fragrances;
fifth, one should not go to visit pleasure pavilions for amusement;
sixth, one should not attend performances by musicians or entertainers.
Seventh, one should neither sing nor dance;
eighth, one should observe the six monthly fasts.
These are the eight matters.
"Furthermore, there are nine matters by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What are these nine?
First, there is nothing to be abandoned;
second, there is nothing to which one may become attached;
third, there is no self.
Fourth, not to conceive of a person;
fifth, not to conceive of a life-span;
sixth, not to conceive of a soul.
Seventh, not dwelling on the place of birth;
eighth, not dwelling on the place of non-birth;
ninth, merely being detached from the twelve links of dependent origination.
These are the nine matters.
Furthermore, there are ten matters by which a woman may quickly attain manhood and personally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
What are the ten?
First, to possess compassion for all beings;
second, not to covet any person or thing.
Third, not to dwell on the male bodies of others;
fourth, not to engage in double-tongued speech;
fifth, not to engage in harsh speech.
Sixth, not speaking falsely;
seventh, not engaging in frivolous speech;
eighth, when others provide him with music and entertainment, he does not take pleasure in them.
Ninth, one neither gives rise to intentional thoughts nor harbors resentment, but simply abides in correctness;
tenth, one does not engage in meritorious acts based on improper causes and conditions to seek association with others.
"These are the ten matters.

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, Bhadraśrī and sixty thousand female lay disciples (*upāsikā*) from the kingdom of Magadha, having heard this Dharma practice, all resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. The various bodhisattvas, including Maitreya, as well as the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and others, placed their heads upon the ground before him, paid homage to the Buddha, and departed with joy.
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Wise Leader (Bhadramukha-sūtra)
